scenes.title: 소수 신규 공격 사례에 대응하는 IDS
scenes.notes: IDS is a classifier of flow records, not a name for the dataset. Begin with the operational gap: only some attack labels are available initially; investigation later supplies a few examples of another attack. The research question is how much newly labelled data and update computation each method needs, while tracking existing-class quality. Do not infer a universal need for retraining from a weekday collection schedule. Full cumulative XGB refitting is our chosen baseline. This experiment evaluates adaptation after labelling, not unknown-attack detection before labelling or generalization across networks.

scenes.title: 평가 데이터 구성 · 출처와 제공 사례의 구분
scenes.notes: Data trace: EXP77 data manifests -> EXP71 cumulative run data -> conflict-free fixed-split manifests. The stored suite may contain multiple benchmark keys, but the experiment selects one dataset independently; no CIC attacks are injected into ToN or vice versa. The 100-row example explains the old setting; the next page explicitly states it has no operational or optimality justification. Original row IDs are disjoint across train/test, but duplicate feature vectors can exist; this is not a claim of feature-disjoint holdout. Stages control which labels become available and how many; the researcher does not synthesize the network-feature rows.

scenes.title: 평가 시나리오 · 신규 공격당 라벨 수 n
scenes.notes: Counts and class arrival order from EXP77/EXP71 manifests. Initial total 750+125+125=1000. The n rows are real labelled training examples, not daily attack frequencies or test counts. Both methods receive the same IDs. Cumulative final sizes: CIC 1000+4n, ToN 1000+7n. Old displayed results sweep n=10/20/50/100/200/400, and the old cost snapshot uses n=100. 100 is an illustrative setting, not a statistical midpoint, optimum, or measured operational frequency. The revised n=5/10/20/30/50 buffer plan is design-only and has no results yet.

items.text: 평가 시나리오 · 신규 공격당 라벨 수 n
아래 수량 = 해당 단계에 새로 제공한 학습/context 사례 · 공격 도입 단계순
n = 100 예시 · CIC 총 1,400개 / ToN 총 1,700개 · 하루 공격량이 아닌 확보 라벨 수
기존 결과 n = 10·20·50·100·200·400 · 100개는 최적값이 아닌 설명용 조건
